title: MANIBELA extends transport strike until Wednesday, November 25, 2026
summary: The Samahang Manibela, Mananakay, at Nagkaisang Terminal ng Transportasyon (MANIBELA) will continue its transport strike until Wednesday, November 25, its leader said Tuesday.

blocks.text: The Samahang Manibela, Mananakay, at Nagkaisang Terminal ng Transportasyon (MANIBELA) will continue its transport strike until Wednesday, November 25, its leader said Tuesday.
“Hanggang bukas, sasalubungin natin. Wala tayong biyahe. Magmamartsa na tayo papunta roon,” MANIBELA chairperson Mar Valbuena said in a video posted on the group’s Facebook page.
(Until tomorrow, we will address them. We have no operations. We will march to that place.)
MANIBELA on Tuesday staged its second day of protest near the Malacañang gate in Nagtahan, Manila.
Valbuena said participating jeepney drivers would remain off the roads as they protest what he described as the appointment of alleged corrupt officials to government positions.

He criticized alleged corruption and irregularities involving the Land Transportation Office (LTO), including transactions involving Dermalog and Paynamics, as well as alleged excessive fees, kickbacks, and payolas.
Members from different MANIBELA chapters had gathered in Nagtahan to bring their concerns to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
After holding a program in the area, the group planned to march toward the LTO office to continue its protest.

Meanwhile, the Manila Police District (MPD) deployed a mobile patrol unit and a pickup truck at the MANIBELA terminal in Nagtahan to provide free rides to commuters affected by the transport strike, according to a report of Manny Vargas on Super Radyo dzBB.

The Manila Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Department said the strike had no significant impact on the city, citing the sufficient number of public utility vehicles still operating on affected routes.
On Monday, the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) deployed over 6,000 personnel as MANIBELA started its transport strike. —KG, GMA News
